accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England Years 3–4 working scientifically statements (use results to draw simple conclusions; use straightforward scientific evidence to answer questions) and the NGSS grades 3–5 practice 'constructing explanations'. Science facts checked: dew forms on grass that cools below the dew point on clear nights while paving stays warmer and dry (Met Office guidance on dew), rain wets every surface, water cannot soak through concrete, puddles shrink by evaporation on hot days, steam and breath condense on cold glass, and old milk can spoil in a working fridge. Parameterised answers (2n, 1, n − 1, n − 2) were enumerated by the validator.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented habits in children's reasoning about evidence (Kuhn 1989; Zimmerman 2007): stopping at the first explanation that fits (confirmation bias), offering a true but non-causal fact ('the grass is green'), ruling out an idea no clue has touched, changing two variables at once (warm and watered window plant), and checking a claim by repeating it with no comparison (singing to cress, lucky socks). Each has its own feedback in the lab and the challenge.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed; the highest 6-token Jaccard is 9.8% (shared shell scaffolding with flag_mil.js). 579 Observation vs interpretation (flagobsvs) sorts statements, and 873 Changing your mind with evidence (flagrethink) updates one idea after surprising results. Only this lab has the learner generate rival explanations for one observation, open clues that rule rivals out until one fits all, set up a plant test with light as the only difference, and pick the check that includes a comparison.

lab_teaches.evidence: Five tasks follow the habit in order: list rival explanations (and reject facts that cannot cause the effect); use clues to rule ideas out and keep the one that fits every clue, 'for now'; remove the other explanations from a test so only light differs; compare with and without the cause; then apply the whole method to the shrinking puddle alone. The banner gives the rule only after the learner's taps reach it.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes: only rain makes grass wet' for the wet grass, 'Yes: light is the only difference' for Ben's window plant (water and warmth also differ in the lab), and 'The water evaporated' or 'A dog drank it' for which idea concrete rules out. The idea cards, the plant table and the puddle clues then show the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions (milk, lucky socks, mouldy bread, a scientist's next step, flat tyre, leaning plant), each with two tagged wrong answers: notExplain, firstIdea, noCompare, opinion and unfair. Each tag has its own message, e.g. 'Two things changed at once, so either one could explain the result. Change only one thing.'

readability.evidence: Kid explanation Flesch-Kincaid grade 2.5 (limit 6.5) and adult 7.0 (limit 9.5), checked with learn/readability.py. The kid text uses everyday scenes (wet grass, a path, cress, a dog bowl) and short sentences for 7 to 9 year olds. Lab cards are four to eight words each.

no_filler.evidence: No filler patterns matched. Each kid paragraph does one job: ask why, list explanations, use clues, compare. The adult text gives curriculum links, the five tasks and named mistakes. Explanation overlap with every other lesson is at most 0.6% (873).

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (both themes) and 1200 px desktop for every step before and after Show me: idea cards in a 2-column grid about 44 px tall, three clue tiles across with 11 px labels, five full-width idea rows and a 5-row plant table all fit without clipping. The canvas is taller on phones (tall 1.25) so the three-line feedback footer does not cover the cards.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a button twin: one button per idea card, 'Clue: …' and 'Rule out: …' buttons, a 'make the same/different' button per plant row, and the full text of each check option as a button. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the observation, open clues, ideas left or plant settings. walk.cjs: axe clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13, no console errors.
